title: What will be the open market US Dollar/Iranian Toman exchange rate on December 31, 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the open market US Dollar/Iranian Toman exchange rate on December 31, 2026 (Tehran time). One Toman is equal to 10 Rial.

The primary source for this question will be [Bonbast](https://www.bonbast.com/graph).
fine_print: Iran’s official Central Bank rate will not be used as resolution, only the market rate.
background:
On August 24, 2026, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced [a new round of sanctions on Iran](https://apnews.com/article/iran-rial-currency-bessent-trade-august-24-2026-e367634d8853c8fa4a341132cd577f31) and warned countries to server financial ties with the Islamic Republic. A week earlier President Trump stated he would impose an ["economic D-Day"](https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-trump-sanctions-economic-fury-oil-d28206ea288a3d4a9b82260ab44ce460) on Iran as significant sanctions continue to affect the Iranian regime despite no end to the war.

The ongoing conflict has led to the Iranian Rial to drop to [a historic low of 2.02 million to the US dollar](https://apnews.com/article/iran-rial-currency-bessent-trade-august-24-2026-e367634d8853c8fa4a341132cd577f31) on currency markets. On January 1, 2026, the open market rate was [around 1.35 million Iranian Rial to the US Dollar](https://www.bonbast.com/graph), with a decline of around a third since then.

comments.author: Theomachado
comments.text:
**Setup:** Bonbast reached 237,500 on 11 September, up 76% year-to-date and 27% in the past 60 days, averaging approximately 11% monthly growth since July. The upper bound is 5.3% away with 111 days remaining. Consumer price inflation is 3.4% month-over-month (89% year-over-year). Crude exports are near zero due to the blockade, and new Treasury designations are issued weekly. Since 18 August, the UAE has suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Dubai's dirham remittance rate, which effectively sets the Tehran dollar price, has created an additional supply shock amid ongoing market panic.

**Market outlook (Polymarket, 11 September): There is a 64% probability the US will announce the end of the blockade by 31 December (37% by 31 October, 21% by 30 September). The likelihood of** Hormuz traffic returning to normal by year-end is 19%. There is a 91% chance there will be no US–Iran diplomatic meeting by 30 September. The Israel–Iran ceasefire is expected to hold through year-end with a 62% probability. The probability of a US invasion of Iran before 2027 is 16%. Overall, markets anticipate a de-escalation *announcement* in the fourth quarter, but do not expect a full reopening or imminent diplomatic talks.

**Why the rate is likely to remain above 250,000. Market rallies tend to be short-lived. For example, the June memorandum of understanding reduced the rate from approximately 179,000 to 153,000 (a 14% drop), but it rebounded to nearly 172,000** within two weeks before hostilities resumed. Similarly, the April truce led to a 15% decline that lasted about a month before the May spike. Based on my estimates, the de-escalation scenario (about 40%, reflecting Polymarket odds adjusted for timing) results in a rate within the 220,000–250,000 range about half the time. A gradual increase scenario (about 45%) would see the rate reach approximately 290,000, while escalation (about 15%, matching invasion odds) could push it to around 420,000. Historical data supports this: since 2018, after a 20% increase over 60 days, the median forward 111-day move was 11%, with gains of 28% to 61% occurring more often than reversals.

**Why the probability is not 80%. Tehran-based analysts project a rate of 240,000–250,000 by late December and 250,000–300,000 only by March 2027, implying monthly growth of 1–3% and suggesting** the current level is an overshoot. The only institutional end-2026 forecast I found, from mid-August when the spot rate was about 188,000, was approximately 180,000. While this is outdated, the consensus view is stabilization rather than further acceleration. The Central Bank of Iran holds around \$4.5 billion purchased from the market, has pledged \$2 billion in interventions, and has already intervened in exchange shops. Additionally, former President Trump may seek a headline related to gasoline prices before 3 November.



***

### **Personal assessment:**

Hormuz leverage has become critical for Tehran, so I anticipate maximalist demands through the midterm elections, followed by a series of announcements with limited substantive change later in the year, which are likely to fade. The primary risk is a genuine reopening in October with asset unfreezing, which could result in a 10–15% decline within days that persists. There is also a resolution risk of a 2018-style shutdown that leaves Bonbast inactive; the late-August crackdown did not prevent continued quoting.
